title.narrative: Indicator 13: increase in installed renewable energy capacity from community-scale systems (e.g., biomass, micro-hydro, solar, etc.)

description.narrative: This indicator measures the increase in renewable energy generation capacity installed through community-scale systems as a result of project interventions. It captures the deployment, expansion, or upgrading of renewable energy technologies that provide clean, reliable, and sustainable energy services for households, communities, local enterprises, and public facilities. The indicator reflects contributions to reducing greenhouse gas emissions, increasing energy access, and strengthening local energy resilience.

title.narrative: Indicator 12: number of locally adapted solutions promoting low-carbon technologies (such as new/modified biogas technology, locally developed energy efficient stoves, innovatives uses of solar/wind energy, etc.)

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of innovative low-carbon technology solutions that have been developed, modified, adapted, tested, or adopted to address local needs and conditions while contributing to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and dependence on fossil fuels. It captures community-driven and locally appropriate technologies that enhance energy efficiency, increase the use of renewable energy, or promote sustainable production and consumption practices.

title.narrative: 23: Number of knowledge exchange/sharing events with participation of local communities

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of knowledge exchange and knowledge-sharing events conducted with the active participation of local communities as a result of project support. These events facilitate the sharing of experiences, lessons learned, best practices, innovations, traditional knowledge, and technical information related to environmental conservation, sustainable livelihoods, climate resilience, natural resource management, and sustainable development.

title.narrative: Indicator 14: Number of local to global coalitions for chemicals and waste management strengthened and or established.

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of multi-stakeholder coalitions, partnerships, networks, platforms, or alliances focused on chemicals and waste management that have been established or strengthened through project support. These coalitions may operate at local, national, regional, or global levels and facilitate collaboration, knowledge exchange, policy dialogue, capacity development, advocacy, and coordinated action to address chemicals, hazardous waste, plastics, electronic waste, and other pollution-related challenges.

title.narrative: Indicator 8: Number of representatives from social inclusion group (indigenous people, women, youth, persons with disability, farmers, other marginalized groups) meaningfully engage in multi-stakeholder dialogue platforms

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of representatives from social inclusion groups who actively and meaningfully participate in multi-stakeholder dialogue platforms supported by the project. It captures the extent to which traditionally underrepresented and marginalized groups are engaged in consultations, planning, decision-making processes, policy discussions, knowledge-sharing events, and governance mechanisms related to environmental sustainability and community development. Meaningful engagement refers to participation that enables individuals to express their views, contribute to discussions, influence decisions, and take part in collective actions, rather than simply attending meetings.

title.narrative: Indicator 10: Number of CSO-government-private sector dialogues formed or strengthened

description.narrative: his indicator measures the number of formal or informal dialogue mechanisms, platforms, forums, working groups, partnerships, or engagement processes involving civil society organizations (CSOs), government institutions, and private sector actors that have been established or strengthened through project support. The indicator captures efforts to enhance multi-stakeholder collaboration, coordination, information exchange, joint problem-solving, and collective action on environmental sustainability, climate change, natural resource management, chemicals and waste management, and sustainable development issues.

title.narrative: 25: Number of projects with meetings involving local CSOs/CBOs or communities to monitor project results, assess impacts, and identify lessons learned

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of projects that conduct meetings involving local civil society organizations (CSOs), community-based organizations (CBOs), and/or community representatives to review project progress, monitor results, assess environmental and socio-economic impacts, and identify lessons learned during implementation. These meetings provide opportunities for stakeholders to participate in project oversight, validate results, share experiences, identify challenges, and contribute recommendations for adaptive management and future interventions.
